To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the austenitisation temperature has a strong influence on the precipitation of carbides/borocarbides in the quenched boron steel.
the formation of carbides in the steel is affected by the austenitisation temperature.
the formation of carbides/borocarbides is affected by the austenitising temperature and the content of boron in the steel.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of boron and austenitization on the precipitation of carbides in quenched low carbon boron steels.
the effect of austentization temperature on the precipitation of carbide/boron carbide in low carbon boron steels after quenching.
the effect of austentization temperature on the microstructure and mechanical properties of low-carbon boron steel.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the austenitized temperature of 105 °C is recommended to be used for the production of low carbon borated steel.

the austenitizating temperature of 10500 °C is optimal for the formation of a high percentage of martensitic microstructure with a minimum of borocarbides on the grain boundaries, which is the main reason for the best mechanical properties of the quenched steel.
the austenitizating temperature of 105 °C is the optimum temperature to obtain the highest tensile strength, hardness and ductility of low carbon boride steel.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the austenitizating at 1050 ºC was more efficient than 1200 ºC and 870ºC in terms of the reduction of the carbides and borocarbides on the grain boundaries, and also, it was more efficient to obtain the highest percentage of the martensite.
austenitization at 1050 ° C was the optimum temperature for the production of low carbon borated steel.

the austenitizaiton temperature of 105 °C is the most suitable temperature to produce a high content of martensitic microstructure and low content of carbide/boro-carbide on the grain boundary, and consequently the highest tensile properties of low carbon steel.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the austenitisation temperature of 10500 °C is recommended to obtain the best combination of mechanical properties and the lowest content of borocarbonate (Fe23(C, B)6).
the austenitizating temperature of 10500 °C was the optimum for obtaining a microstructure that was free of grain boundary precipitates, and the best mechanical properties of the steel.
boron has a significant effect on the reduction of the formation of the carbide/borcarbide in the steel.
